newsitem.title: USA: Mexico's Zedillo sees drug trade as biggest threat.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Zedillo sees drug trade as biggest threat.

text.p: Drug smuggling represents the biggest threat to Mexico's national security, President Ernesto Zedillo told the Washington Post in an interview published on Wednesday.

Citing drug-related killings across the country, including the assassinations of seven federal prosecutors in Tijuana, Zedillo vowed to combat traffickers but placed much of the blame for Mexico's drug plague at the doorstep of the United States.
"As long as we have such strong demand (in the United States) and such huge profit margins, unfortunately there will be the incentive for drug trafficking," he said.
Nevertheless, Zedillo told the newspaper in an interview on Monday in Mexico City, he rejected the notion that Mexico could become as drug-ridden as Colombia.
"I can tell you with all confidence, absolute confidence, that there is no way in which we can approach the situation that has unfortunately (occurred) in Colombia," he said.

Zedillo told the Post that fighting drug traffickers in Mexico had been difficult because "these people have lots of mobility, they have lots of resources and we know that they have been able - not now, but a long time ago - to penetrate the police structures."
He said that "at some level" they might still have people in police positions.

"If we don't keep a constant struggle against drug trafficking, then drug trafficking - not only in Mexico, but in many other countries - will become an effective threat to our institutions, to our everyday life," Zedillo said.
